questions.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ on $M?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3+(3)(-1) & -1+(3)(2) & 9+(3)(4)\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 21\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.:question/problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the second row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}0+(-2)(5) & 4+(-2)(2) & 7+(-2)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(1)(5) & 3+(1)(2) & 0+(1)(1)\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 5 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ on $B?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $G,$ given by

$$
G=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2}$ on $G?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $-5$ times the second row to the third row. 

Applying this row operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}G & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0+(-5)(0) & 5+(-5)(1) & 6+(-5)(2)\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix}
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_2 := R_2 +(- 4) \cdot R_1$ on $A?$
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_2:=R_2 + (-4) R_1$ means that we need to add $-4$ times the first row to the second row. 

Carrying out this row operation, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4+(-4)(1) & 2+(-4)(2) & -1+(-4)(3) \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & -13 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
